name: Jeremiah
overview: Jeremiah was a male Aaronic priest from the tribe of Levi, identified in Nehemiah 10:2 as a signatory on a sealed document. His priestly lineage connects him to the sacred duties established under the Mosaic covenant. This background situates him within the Levitical priesthood during a critical period of Israel's history.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeremiah means 'Yahweh loosens [the womb]' or 'Yahweh lifts up,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's active role in deliverance or establishment. This proper name is recorded in Nehemiah 10:2 and does not appear to have been given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture infers that Jeremiah was a descendant of Aaron, affirming his priestly heritage (Nehemiah 10:2). Additionally, Hananiah is identified as his father in Nehemiah 12:12, providing a direct familial link within the Levitical line.
scriptureSignificance: Jeremiah's role as an Aaronic priest places him within the covenantal framework of Israel's worship and law. His inclusion on the sealed document in Nehemiah 10 highlights his active participation in the community's commitment to God's covenant. His priestly identity and documented lineage underscore his importance in the restoration efforts and spiritual leadership during Israel's post-exilic period.
